page: Google Cloud Platform g1-small is a shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the g1 family. It features 1 vCPU mapped to a shared physical core on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 2.0 GB of total system memory, providing approximately 1.7 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Due to its shared-core architecture, the g1-small exhibits limited compute and memory throughput. Benchmark data places its stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance at 1076.89, which falls into the bottom tier of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, measuring 10.49 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 8.91 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Cryptographic and compression tasks also reflect this low-resource profile, with gzip compression executing at 18.57 GB/sec and Passmark CPU encryption scoring 401.65.

The primary tradeoff of the g1-small is its highly constrained performance in exchange for a budget-friendly resource profile. With a Passmark database score of 564.91 and Redis SET performance at 0.59 million operations per second, this instance is unsuitable for production databases or high-traffic applications. It is best utilized for low-intensity workloads such as basic static web serving, lightweight development environments, microservices, or simple background cron jobs that do not require sustained CPU utilization.
